# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei ist Teil des Kuratierungsprozesses: Sie enthält die inhaltlichen
Leitplanken für alle KI-generierten Texte und Diagramme. Die maschinenlesbaren
Parameter dazu stehen in `ai/policy.json`; beide werden von

Änderungen an Policy oder Richtlinien ⇒ `version` in `policy.json` erhöhen;
`ai_workflow.py status` zeigt dann, welche Fragmente noch mit einer älteren
Version erzeugt wurden.

## Geltungsbereich und Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch (`site.json → sprachen.kanonisch`). KI-Inhalte
  werden ausschließlich deutsch erzeugt; die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter
  Schritt (i18n_*.py) und niemals Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und `[SWS_…]`-Kennungen bleiben
  in jeder Sprache unverändert.

## Strukturelle Invarianten

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai` für
  Abschnitte, `ai usage` für Verwendungshinweise an Records, `ai module-guide`
  für Modul-Leitfäden) mit Badge und abschließender `<p class="ai-note">`
  (KI-Hinweis). Bestehende Fragmente sind die Referenz.
- Fragmente liegen unter `content/ai/<seiten-verzeichnis>/` und heißen
  `rec_<ELEMENT-ID>_<NN>.html` (an ein Spezifikationselement gebunden) oder
  `main_<NN>.html` (seitenbezogen).

## Belegpflicht und Quellen

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist mit `[SWS_…]`/`[RS_…]`-Zitat zu belegen
  (`policy.zitierpflicht`); Zitate verlinken auf das Quelldokument (PDF mit
  `#nameddest`), Richtwert `policy.relevanz.min_zitate_je_absatz`.
- Es dürfen nur Dokumente aus dem Quellenregister `ai/quellen.json` verwendet
  werden. Neue Quellen werden zuerst dort registriert (id, titel, typ, url).
- Aus Quellen extrahierte Einzelaussagen, auf die sich ein Text stützt, werden
  in der Trace unter `wissen[]` festgehalten: `{"aussage": …, "quelle": <id>,
  "fundstelle": …}`.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Spezifikation schweigt, darf die KI Lücken mit Annahmen schließen —
  höchstens `policy.annahmen.budget_je_text` pro Text bzw.
  `budget_je_diagramm` pro Diagramm.
- Jede Annahme wird (a) im Text als Interpretation erkennbar formuliert und
  (b) in der Trace unter `annahmen[]` protokolliert:
  `{"annahme": …, "begruendung": …}`.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekuliert.

## Diagramm-Entscheidung

Ein Diagramm wird nur eingefügt, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet
(`policy.diagramme`):

- Sequenzdiagramm (`.seq.json`): Abläufe mit ≥ `sequenz_ab_schritten`
  Schritten oder nicht offensichtlicher Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Strukturdiagramm (`.dot`): ≥ `kontext_ab_beteiligten` beteiligte
  Komponenten oder nicht-triviale Vererbungs-/Abhängigkeitscluster.
- Zustandsdiagramm (`.dot`): Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Die Entscheidung („warum dieses Diagramm, warum diese Form“), etwaige
Annahmen und das Denk-Transkript zur Quellenerstellung gehören in die Trace
unter `diagramme["<quellpfad>"]` — nicht ins HTML. Diagrammquellen liegen als
`<fragment-stem>.<diag-id>.dot|.seq.json` neben dem Fragment (inline) bzw.
unter `diagrams/` (seitenweite Diagramme); gerendert wird mit
`render_diagrams.py`. Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert.

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Network Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n1 Introduction and functional overview\nThis specification describes the functionality, API and the configuration of the\nNetwork\nManagement\nfor the AUTOSAR\nAdaptive Platform\n.\nAdaptive Network Management (NM) is intended to work independent of the commu-\nnication stack used. Its main purpose is to coordinate the transition between normal\noperation and bus-sleep mode of the underlying networks (physical and partial net-\nworks)."

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Network Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n4 Constraints and assumptions\n4.1 Limitations\nThe Adaptive Network Management is actually only supporting UdpNM.\nThe Adaptive Network Management does not allow node detection (Repeat Message\nState) but only handles incoming requests.\nThe Adaptive Network Management cannot be configured as the master network co-\nordinator.\nThe Adaptive Network Management does not support coordinated shutdown using the\ninformation in CBV.\nThe Adaptive Network Management does not support passive mode and passive start-\nup. Passive start-up would mean that a node has started (i.e. goes to Normal mode),\nbut the network has been woken up by another node.\nModeling part for mapping the logical networks to the BitVector positions as defined in\nchapter 7.3 is not available in the manifest.\nUpdate and access of User Data was removed as the service interface to Applications\nhas been removed. State Management will control the network request/release and it\nmust be clarified if user data changes/indications shall be done via State Management\nor directly by applications.\n4.2 Applicability to car domains\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Network Management can be used for all car domains.\n8 of 30\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 898: AUTOSAR_SWS_NetworkManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Network Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n7 Functional specification\nThe Adaptive Network Management offers services that allow the applications to re-\nquest the necessary network states for logical networks that can be mapped to physical\nor partial networks.\nTo do so, the following functionalities are provided:\n1) Field for requesting and releasing logical networks\n2) Support for partial networking\n7.1 Architectural Overview\nFigure 7.1 gives an overview of the Adaptive NM service.\nThe following figure shows an overview on the interaction between\nState Manage-\nment\nand\nNetwork Management\nas well as an example mapping between logical\nnetworks, partial networks and physical networks."

      "id": "SNIP_nm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_N_P13_25",
      "source_element": "SWS_ANM_00001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement",
      "source_page": 13,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Network Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n7.2 Network Management Algorithm\nThe AUTOSAR Adaptive NM is based on decentralized direct network management\nstrategy, which means that every network node performs activities self-sufficient de-\npending only on the NM packets received and/or transmitted within the communication\nsystem.\nThe AUTOSAR Adaptive NM algorithm is based on periodic NM packets, which are\nreceived by all nodes in the cluster via multicast. Reception of NM packets indicates\nthat sending nodes want to keep the NM-cluster awake. If any node is ready to go\nto sleep mode, it stops sending NM packets, but as long as NM packets from other\nnodes are received, it postpones transition to sleep mode. Finally, if a dedicated timer\nelapses because no NM packets are received anymore, every node initiates transition\nto the sleep mode.\nIf any node in the NM-cluster requires bus-communication, it can keep the NM-cluster\nawake by transmitting NM packets.\nThe main concept of the AUTOSAR Adaptive NM coordination algorithm can be defined\nby the following key-requirement.\n[SWS_ANM_00001]\n⌈\nEvery network node shall transmit periodic NM messages as\nlong as it requires bus-communication; otherwise it shall not transmit NM messages.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00044)\n13 of 30\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 898: AUTOSAR_SWS_NetworkManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_nm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_N_P14_26",
      "source_element": "SWS_ANM_00063",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement",
      "source_page": 14,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Network Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n7.3 NetworkControl\nLogical networks are a mapped to one partial or physical network, while a partial net-\nworks can be mapped to one or multiple physical networks.\nWith the introduction of the\nState Management\nfunctional cluster,\nNetwork Man-\nagement\nno longer receives logical network requests from applications, instead they\nare controlled by the\nState Management\n.\nState Management\ncan split the one or\nmore applications in multiple functions that might require network communication. Ap-\nplications (or part of) would then request different functions to be activated/deactivated\nfrom\nState Management\nand then\nState Management\nwould in turn, depending\non configuration, request/release different logical networks. The end effect being that\none or multiple physical networks are activated/deactivated.\n[SWS_ANM_00063]\n⌈\nEach port offered by\nNM\nshall enable control of single logical\nnetwork.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00050)\n[SWS_ANM_00066]\n⌈\nEach port shall be mapped over the manifest to the logical net-\nworks.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_02522)\n[SWS_ANM_00067]\n⌈\nIn case of partial networking a mapping between partial\nnetwork(s) and physical network(s) needs to be configured.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_02517,\nRS_Nm_02519, RS_Nm_02520)\n[SWS_ANM_00068]\n⌈\nIn case of no partial networking, the mapping will be\ndone between port and physical network(s).\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_02517, RS_Nm_02519,\nRS_Nm_02520)\n14 of 30\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 898: AUTOSAR_SWS_NetworkManagement"
    },

      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement",
      "source_page": 15,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Network Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n7.4 Operational Modes\nThis chapter describes the operational modes of the AUTOSAR Adaptive NM.\n[SWS_ANM_00062]\n⌈\nEach NM Service instance shall realize the state machine men-\ntioned in the figure described below.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00044)\n(Figure 7.2)\nNote: The state machine in Figure 7.2 is applied to physical channels. In case of partial\nnetworking, the Nm module should additionally take care of relevant PNs.\n[SWS_ANM_00004]\n⌈\nThe AUTOSAR Adaptive NM shall contain three operational\nmodes:\n•\nNetwork Mode\n•\nPrepare Bus-Sleep Mode\n•\nBus-Sleep Mode\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00044)\nFor more information check the following chapters:\n•\nNetwork Mode, see 7.4.1\n•\nPrepare Bus-Sleep Mode, see 7.4.2\n•\nBus-Sleep Mode, see 7.4.3\nThese modes will not be visible to the Adaptive Application as it is.\nWhen the NM is in Network mode it implies that the network is requested or active.\nAnd the logical network information bit will be set to 1.\nWhen the NM is in Prepare Bus-Sleep or Bus-Sleep Mode, It implies that the network\nis released or inactive. And the logical network information bit will be set to 0.\nThe following figure shows the state diagram. Mode change related transitions are\ndenoted in green and error handling related transmissions in red.\n15 of 30\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 898: AUTOSAR_SWS_NetworkManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Network Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n[SWS_ANM_00006]\n⌈\nWhen the Network Mode is entered from Bus-Sleep Mode or\nPrepare Bus-Sleep Mode, by default, the Repeat Message State shall be entered.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00044)\n[SWS_ANM_00007]\n⌈\nWhen the Network Mode is entered, the NM-Timeout Timer\nshall be started with the value\nNmTimeoutTime\n.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00044, RS_Nm_00150)\n[SWS_ANM_00008]\n⌈\nUpon successful reception of a NM message in Network\nMode, the NM-Timeout Timer shall be restarted with the value NmTimeoutTime.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00044)\n[SWS_ANM_00009]\n⌈\nUpon successful transmission of a NM message in Network\nMode, the NM-Timeout Timer shall be restarted with the value NmTimeoutTime.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00044)\n7.4.1.1 Repeat Message State\nThe Repeat Message State ensures, that any transition from Bus-Sleep or Prepare\nBus-Sleep to the Network Mode becomes visible for the other nodes on the network.\nAdditionally, it ensures that any node stays active for a minimum amount of time.\n[SWS_ANM_00011]\n⌈\nWhen the Repeat Message State of Network Mode is entered\nfrom Bus-Sleep Mode, Prepare-Bus-Sleep Mode or from within Network Mode (Normal\nOperation State or Ready Sleep State) transmission of NM messages shall be (re-)\nstarted.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00047)\n[SWS_ANM_00012]\n⌈\nWhen the NM-Timeout Timer expires in the Repeat Message\nState, the NM-Timeout Timer shall be restarted.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00044)\n[SWS_ANM_00013]\n⌈\nThe NM shall stay in the Repeat Message State for a config-\nurable amount of time determined by the\nNmRepeatMessageTime\n; after that time the\nRepeat Message State shall be left.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00044, RS_Nm_00150)\n[SWS_ANM_00014]\n⌈\nWhen Repeat Message State is left, the Normal Operation State\nshall be entered, if the network has been requested.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00047)\n[SWS_ANM_00015]\n⌈\nWhen Repeat Message State is left, the Ready Sleep State\nshall be entered, if the network has been released.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00047)\n[SWS_ANM_00070]\n⌈\nThe Repeat Message State of Network Mode is entered from\nBus-Sleep Mode or Prepare-Bus-Sleep Mode by default, when a logical network is\nrequested using RequestNetwork method and the NM module shall transmit a NM\nmessage immediately.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00044)\n17 of 30\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 898: AUTOSAR_SWS_NetworkManagement"

and the Prepare Bus-Sleep Mode shall be entered.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00044)\n[SWS_ANM_00022]\n⌈\nWhen the network is requested and the current state is the\nReady Sleep State, the Ready Sleep State shall be left and the Normal Operation\nState shall be entered.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00047)\n[SWS_ANM_00023]\n⌈\nIf Repeat Message Request Bit (set in the CBV of the received\nNM message) is received in the Ready Sleep       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Network Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n7.4.2 Prepare Bus-Sleep Mode\nThe purpose of the Prepare Bus Sleep state is to ensure that all nodes have time to\nstop their network activity before the Bus Sleep state is entered. Bus activity is calmed\ndown (i.e. queued messages are transmitted in order to empty all TX-buffers) and\nfinally there is no activity on the bus in the Prepare Bus-Sleep Mode.\n[SWS_ANM_00024]\n⌈\nThe NM shall stay in the Prepare Bus-Sleep Mode for an amount\nof time determined by the\nNmWaitBusSleepTime\n; after that time, the Prepare Bus-\nSleep Mode shall be left and the Bus-Sleep Mode shall be entered.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00048,\nRS_Nm_00054)\n[SWS_ANM_00025]\n⌈\nUpon successful reception of a NM message in the Prepare\nBus-Sleep Mode, the Prepare Bus-Sleep Mode shall be left and the Network Mode\nshall be entered; by default, the Repeat Message State is entered.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00047)\nRationale: Other nodes in the cluster are still in Prepare Bus-Sleep Mode; in the excep-\ntional situation described above, transition into the Bus-Sleep Mode shall be avoided\nand bus-communication shall be restored as fast as possible.\n7.4.3 Bus-Sleep Mode\nThe purpose of the Bus-Sleep state is to reduce power consumption in the node, when\nno messages are to be exchanged. Transmission and reception capabilities can be\nswitched off if supported by hardware.\nIf a configurable amount of time determined by\nNmTimeoutTime\n+\nNmWaitBus-\nSleepTime\nis identically configured for all nodes in the network management clus-\nter, all nodes in the network management cluster that are coordinated with use of the\nAUTOSAR NM algorithm perform the transition into the Bus-Sleep Mode at approxi-\nmately the same time.\n[SWS_ANM_00028]\n⌈\nIf bus communication is released and there are no NM mes-\nsages on the bus for a configurable amount of time, determined by\nNmTimeoutTime\n+\nNmWaitBusSleepTime\n, transition into the Bus-Sleep Mode shall be performed from\nthe Network Mode.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00150)\n[SWS_ANM_00031]\n⌈\nIn the Bus-Sleep Mode the corresponding bit of\nNetwork-\nState BitVector\n, which represents the relevant logical network, shall be 0.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00050)\nNote: In Bus-Sleep Mode, it is assumed that all nodes in a cluster are in this state.\nTypically, all nodes request the communication approximately at the same time by a\ncommon trigger, for instance a wake-up line.\n19 of 30\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 898: AUTOSAR_SWS_NetworkManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Network Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n7.5 Message Format\nMessage Layout is shown in [3], chapter 5.1.\nNote: As mentioned in [3], the length of an NM packet shall not exceed the MTU\n(Maximum Transmission Unit) of the underlying physical transport layer.\n7.5.1 Source Node Identifier\n[SWS_ANM_00033]\n⌈\nThe location of the source node identifier shall be configurable\nusing\nNmPduNidPosition\n, to position Byte 0 or Byte 1 or Off (default: Byte 0).\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00150, RS_Nm_02505)\n[SWS_ANM_00034]\n⌈\nThe source node identifier shall be set with configurable Node-\nId value\nNmNodeId\nunless the location of the source node identifier is set to Off.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_02508, RS_Nm_02505)\n7.5.2 Control Bit Vector\nThe format (bit-layout) and definition of the CBV is shown in [3], chapter 5.1.2 Control\nBit Vector.\n[SWS_ANM_00035]\n⌈\nThe location of the Control Bit Vector shall be configurable us-\ning\nNmPduCbvPosition\n, to position Byte 0 or Byte 1 or Off (default: Byte 1).\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00150)\n[SWS_ANM_00037]\n⌈\nRepeat Message Request Bit shall always be set to 0 in the\ntransmitted NM message.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00151)\n[SWS_ANM_00038]\n⌈\nActive Wakeup Bit shall always be set to 0 in the transmitted NM\nmessage.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00151)\n[SWS_ANM_00071]\n⌈\nNM Coordinator Sleep Ready Bit shall always be set to 0 in the\ntransmitted NM message.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00151)\n7.5.3 User Data\n[SWS_ANM_00039]\n⌈\nIt shall be possible to enable or disable the support of NM user\ndata, using parameter\nNmUserDataEnabled\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_02503, RS_Nm_02504)\n[SWS_ANM_00040]\n⌈\nIf NM user data is configured it will be sent always in the NM\nmessage.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00150)\nNote: the range (in bytes) that contains the user data in the received NM message is\ndefined by\nNmUserDataLength\n.\n20 of 30\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 898: AUTOSAR_SWS_NetworkManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Network Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\n7.8 Partial Networking\n7.8.1 Partial Network State Machine\nThe partial network state machine mentioned in Figure 7.1 is supposed to be imple-\nmentation specific. Note: Although beeing implementation specific, the implemented\nbehaviour shall conform to the Partial Networking requirements described in [3].\n7.8.2 Rx Handling of NM messages\nNote : Reception Handling of PN Information as described in [3] is switched on/off by\nNmPnEnabled\n[SWS_ANM_00051]\n⌈\nIf\nNmPnEnabled\nis\nTRUE\nand the PNI bit in the received NM\nmessage is 1, the NM shall invoke the NetworkHandle Notifier, every time a BitVector\nhas been received in the NM message that leads to a change in the actual request\nstate of a relevant PN or a channel.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00150)\nNote: If\nNmPnEnabled\nis\nTRUE\nand the PNI bit in the received NM message is 0, NM\nmodule still will process the user data information.\n[SWS_ANM_00077]\n⌈\nIf\nNmPnEnabled\nis\nTRUE\n, the getter for the NetworkHandle shall\nprovide the (aggregated) request state of the PNs instead of mirroring the last received\nPartial Network information.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00150)\nNote: PnResetTime specified in [3] shall be configured by\nNmPnResetTime\n. This has\nto be ensured by configuration in the respective platform.\n7.8.4 NM message Filter Algorithm\n[SWS_ANM_00055]\n⌈\nThe range (in bytes) that contains the PN request information\n(PN Info Range) in the received NM message shall be defined by PN Info Offset\n(\nNmPnInfoOffset\n) starting from byte 0 and PN Info Length (\nNmPnInfoLength\n).\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_02520)\nExample:\n•\nPN Info Offset = 3\n24 of 30\n AUTOSAR CONFIDENTIAL \nDocument ID 898: AUTOSAR_SWS_NetworkManagement"

If the bit is set to 0 there is no request for this PN.\nThe Adaptive Application requesting the partial network, shall encode the information in\nthe form of Bit fields and use the methods\nRequestNetwork\nand\nReleaseNetwork\n.\n[SWS_ANM_00081]\n⌈\nThe Nm shall optionally filter out messages containing PN re-\nquest information if they do not contain at least one bit set to 1 that corresponds to a\npnc that is configured for this ECU.\n⌋\n(RS_Nm_00150)\nNote: When activated the Nm\nMessage Filter Algorithm will filter out any Nm Message not containing at least one\nrelevant PN beeing requested (its Bit in the PN vector set to 1).       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Network Management\nAUTOSAR AP Release 18-10\nA Interfaces to other Functional Clusters (informative)\nA.1 Overview\nAUTOSAR decided not to standardize interfaces which are exclusively used between\nFunctional Clusters (on platform-level only), to allow efficient implementations, which\nmight depend e.g. on the used Operating System.\nThis chapter provides informative guidelines how the interaction between Functional\nClusters looks like, by clustering the relevant requirements of this document to describe\nInter-Functional Cluster (IFC) interfaces. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h3>Rolle & Verwendungszweck</h3><p>Das funktionale Cluster Network Management (NM) in der AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform koordiniert den Kommunikationszustand logischer und physischer Netzwerke. Es ermöglicht den energieeffizienten Betrieb des Gesamtfahrzeugs, indem nicht benötigte Bussysteme, Teilnetze (Partial Networks, PNC) und VLANs selektiv in den Ruhezustand (Bus-Sleep) versetzt oder bedarfsgerecht aufgeweckt werden. Die primäre Schnittstelle zur Plattform bildet die Klasse <code>ara::nm::NetworkHandle</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_01000\">[SWS_ANM_01000]</a>, deren primärer autorisierter Konsument im Architekturmodell das funktionale Cluster State Management (SM) ist <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.3\">SWS Network Management §7.3 „NetworkControl“</a>.</p><h3>Architektur- und Schnittstellenverträge</h3><p>Ein logisches Netzwerk wird anwendungsintern durch eine Instanz von <code>NetworkHandle</code> gekapselt, die über einen wohldefinierten <code>ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</code> konstruiert wird <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_01001\">[SWS_ANM_01001]</a>. Das Handle-Objekt unterliegt strikten Besitzsemantiken: Kopierkonstruktor und Kopierzuweisungsoperator sind explizit gelöscht <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_01005\">[SWS_ANM_01005]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_01006\">[SWS_ANM_01006]</a>, während Move-Konstruktion und Move-Zuweisung unterstützt werden <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_01003\">[SWS_ANM_01003]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_01004\">[SWS_ANM_01004]</a>.</p><p>Die Schnittstelle trennt strikt zwischen dem angeforderten Wunschzustand und dem tatsächlich synchronisierten Netzwerkzustand:</p><ul><li><code>SetNetworkRequestedState(requestedState)</code> übermittelt den geforderten Zielzustand (z. B. <code>kFullCom</code>) asynchron an den NM-Stack <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_01009\">[SWS_ANM_01009]</a>.</li><li><code>GetNetworkRequestedState()</code> fragt den aktuell für das Handle registrierten Anforderungswert ab <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_01008\">[SWS_ANM_01008]</a>.</li><li><code>GetNetworkState()</code> liefert den tatsächlich erreichten Netzwerkzustand zurück <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_01007\">[SWS_ANM_01007]</a>. Hierbei signalisiert der Enumerator <code>kFullCom</code> erst dann volle Einsatzbereitschaft, wenn alle dem Handle zugeordneten physischen Kanäle und partiellen Netze aktiv synchronisiert sind <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_00083\">[SWS_ANM_00083]</a>.</li><li>Über <code>RegisterNetworkStateChangeNotifier(...)</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_01010\">[SWS_ANM_01010]</a> bzw. <code>RegisterNetworkRequestedStateChangeNotifier(...)</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_01012\">[SWS_ANM_01012]</a> können Rückruffunktionen vom Typ <code>NetworkStateChangeNotifier</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_01020\">[SWS_ANM_01020]</a> registriert werden, um Zustandsübergänge reaktiv ohne Polling zu verarbeiten.</li></ul><h3>Interaktionsfluss</h3><p>Der dezentrale AUTOSAR-NM-Algorithmus basiert auf dem periodischen Austausch von NM-Botschaften (PDUs). Beim Übergang aus dem Ruhemodus (Bus-Sleep Mode) wechselt der Stack über den Repeat Message State in den Normal Operation State <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_00005\">[SWS_ANM_00005]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_00006\">[SWS_ANM_00006]</a>. Eine Anforderung von <code>kFullCom</code> sorgt dafür, dass die NM-Botschaften fortlaufend gesendet und die relevanten Partial Network Bits gesetzt werden, wodurch das Cluster aktiv gehalten wird <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_NetworkManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_ANM_00084\">[SWS_ANM_00084]</a>. Entfällt die Anforderung (Übergang zu <code>kNoCom</code>), wechselt der Knoten in den Ready Sleep State und wartet auf das Timeout des NM-Nachrichtenfensters, bevor der Bus-Sleep-Modus eingeleitet 7.2 Network Management Algorithm
The AUTOSAR Adaptive NM is based on decentralized direct network management
strategy, which means that every network node performs activities self-sufficient de-
pending only on the NM packets received and/or transmitted within the communication
system.
The AUTOSAR Adaptive NM algorithm is based on periodic NM packets, which are
received by all nodes in the cluster via multicast. Reception of NM packets indicates
that sending nodes want to keep the NM-cluster awake. If any node is ready to go
to sleep mode, it stops sending NM packets, but as long as NM packets from other
nodes are received, it postpones transition to sleep mode. Finally, if a dedicated timer
elapses because no NM packets are received anymore, every node initiates transition
to the sleep mode.
If any node in the NM-cluster requires bus-communication, it can keep the NM-cluster
awake by transmitting NM packets.
The main concept of the AUTOSAR Adaptive NM coordination algorithm can be defined
by the following key-requirement.

⌈
Every network node shall transmit periodic NM messages as
long as it requires bus-communication; otherwise it shall not transmit NM messages.

7.4.2 Prepare Bus-Sleep Mode
The purpose of the Prepare Bus Sleep state is to ensure that all nodes have time to
stop their network activity before the Bus Sleep state is entered. Bus activity is calmed
down (i.e. queued messages are transmitted in order to empty all TX-buffers) and
finally there is no activity on the bus in the Prepare Bus-Sleep Mode.

AUTOSAR decided not to standardize interfaces which are exclusively used between
